summary: SPP files its 30-day informational report on resource adequacy for new large loads. It reports a 2026 summer reserve margin of 17.1 percent, describes its ERAS, Provisional Load, HILL, CHILLS and planning reforms, and sets a schedule for the PAL/PALS flexible-load proposal.

points.point: SPP lists complementary initiatives it says have improved planning, resource addition and large load integration.
points.quote: SPP has developed complementary initiatives that improve planning certainty, accelerate the addition of new resources, enhance operational flexibility, strengthen resource adequacy accountability

points.point: SPP's East balancing area shows a 17.1 percent summer 2026 reserve margin, about 5,752 MW above requirements.
points.quote: the East BAA maintains a reserve margin of 17.1%, representing approximately 5,752 MW of excess accredited capacity above the total RAR.

points.point: At the ERAS filing SPP predicted a 2-3 GW accredited capacity shortfall by 2030.
points.quote: SPP predicted that the SPP Region could face a 2-3 GW accredited capacity shortfall by 2030.

points.point: ERAS has 36 active requests representing about 13.3 GW, with none withdrawn.
points.quote: there are 36 active ERAS requests representing approximately 13.3 GW of generating capacity and no requests have withdrawn.

points.point: SPP defines HILLs at 10 MW or more at 69 kV and below, or 50 MW or more above 69 kV.
points.quote: 50 MW or more if connected to the Transmission System at a voltage level greater than 69 kV

points.point: PALS would be a non-firm service with usage-based billing for fully dispatchable loads subject to curtailment.
points.quote: PALS would utilize a usage-based billing structure and require participating loads to be fully dispatchable

points.point: PAL/PALS faces MOPC and RSC votes on October 13 and November 16, with a FERC filing by November 16, 2026.
points.quote: final votes by MOPC on October 13, 2026, and the RSC on November 16, 2026.

throughLine.text: Answers the E-9 30-day directive for an informational report on resource adequacy for large loads and gives the stakeholder schedule for the PAL/PALS service the order cites for flexible loads.

figures.quote: approximately 5,752 MW of excess accredited capacity above the total RAR
